Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and a few asks from procurement/security: 

Q1: Hosted API would be acceptable only if we get contractual guarantees that data-at-rest (including backups and snapshots) remain in the EU and that there is no automatic cross-region replication. We also need encryption keys to be customer-controlled (KMS/HSM) or a strong key management option.

Q2: Dedicated capacity sounds promising — procurement prefers a dedicated tenancy in eu-central-1 if it means stronger isolation and control over backups. Private VPC is acceptable but procurement will ask for clear lead times and whether there are on-prem options for a later phase.

Q3: Procurement timeline — we aim to have a vendor decision by end of August and formal contracting (PO + DPA) by mid-September. SOC2 summary would be good to start our security checklist.

Additional asks:
- Can you provide estimated p95 latency numbers for Hosted in eu-central-1 for our workload (short context: typical prompt lengths ~400 tokens, response ~150 tokens)?
- Is there an option to route EU traffic to a dedicated region while allowing APAC users to hit a different model endpoint without copying EU data? We want to avoid replicating PII outside the EU.

I'll review the SOC2 doc this afternoon and loop in our legal if the DPA looks standard.

—Emma

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear notes. A few technical clarifications and options that map to your procurement preferences: 

Short answers: 
- Hosted API (eu region): we can ensure data-at-rest and backups remain in the chosen EU region (we support eu-central-1). Cross-region replication is not enabled by default; we can disable multi-region replication in the hosting config. Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private VPC. For Hosted API we offer KMS integration via Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) in enterprise plans — we should confirm with legal if that meets your KMS requirement.

- Dedicated capacity: gives you a reserved GPU pool in eu-central-1, stronger tenancy isolation, predictable p99/p95 latencies, and the ability to pin model versions. Backups and snapshots can be kept in-region and lifecycle policies configured to avoid cross-region copy. This is often the procurement-preferred middle-ground.

- Private VPC / on-prem: supports customer-controlled networking, HSM/KMS integration, and air-gapped on-prem installs. Typical VPC provisioning lead time: 4–6 weeks once we have networking and security prescreens completed; on-prem channel delivery can take 10–14+ weeks depending on site ops.

Latency estimates (rough, based on similar workloads):
- Hosted API (eu-central-1): p95 generation ~ 320–420ms for prompts ~400 tokens / response ~150 tokens with continuous batching disabled and single-request routing. With our Dedicated instance sizes and optimized batching p95 can drop to ~240–300ms depending on exact model choice.

Routing options to avoid EU data leaving region:
- Option A (recommended): EU users hit an EU-only endpoint (Hosted or Dedicated) with no cross-region replication; APAC users hit a separate APAC endpoint. User-level routing at the application layer avoids copying EU PII.
- Option B: A single global endpoint with smart routing that strips/redirects PII before it leaves the EU region — requires app-level changes and careful redaction.

Next steps I propose (technical):
- We'll attach a short one-pager that maps Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC to compliance, latency, and timeline. (attached: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf)
- If procurement is leaning Dedicated, we can prepare an initial capacity plan and a timeline for reservation and onboarding.

Attachments: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (PDF), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF)
